issues.issue: Opening question substitutes a horary figure for missing children's recorded birth times; natal chart and horary chart must not be conflated.
Historical vocation taxonomies describe 1647 social occupations and status judgments, not current aptitude prediction accuracy.
The original printed glyphs for the two special profession significators have been independently zoomed and read as Mars and Venus; their essential/accidental strength calculations remain unresolved.
Choosing the stronger planet depends on historical essential/accidental dignity rules not independently computed.
Aries classification invokes four angles and a fiery planet as additional conditions, not unconditional Aries-to-smith mapping.
The author lists many occupations under one sign; retrospective matching and apparent specificity are sensitive to broad category grouping.
An exalted planet is proposed to favor serving the king or nobles; historical class hierarchy is not empirical career advantage.
Five four-footed, three human, and three water-associated signs overlap specific sign occupational lists, and Gemini has a flying-fowl exception.
The water-sign class is explicitly angular in one passage, whereas a vague water association remains even without occupancy.
Taurus 'women's matters' and housewifery are early-modern gender stereotyping, not modern constraints on suitable work.
Some original obsolete occupation terms, including whister, must be kept close to first-edition wording if translated.
Gemini lists scribes, clerks, mathematics, surveyors, astrologers and painters, many independent roles with no verified person.
Leo names heated crafts, cattle healer and transportation roles, and is not a current medical vocational screen.
Virgo includes political, astrological and divining language with broad occupational interpretation rather than testable professional competence.
Libra covers poetry, speech, music, textiles, pedagogy and prisoner redemption; these are not a single occupation class.
Scorpio lists historical medicine and surgery; no safety or clinical fitness conclusion follows.
Sagittarius includes chymistry, religion, cattle trading and cooking, which must not be conflated with modern chemical or medical qualifications.
Capricorn includes farming, country goods, metal and animal-care roles, overlapping other signs.
Aquarius ship work has an additional watery-planet aspect condition for some maritime roles, not merely Aquarius placement.
Pisces text includes disparaging 'dull' or 'sot' judgments about children; record authorial prejudice only, never treat as cognitive diagnosis.
Missing Cancer-specific stand-alone profession list is a source-coverage observation only: Cancer appears in the general water taxonomy; do not invent an omitted rule.
Next LXXXV dated Prince Rupert/Earl of Essex war question begins PDF486; its chart must not enter LXXXIV source annotations.
No named child birth data, independently documented profession, prospective prediction, controls or modern validation appears in the two chapter pages.
No original complete independent diplomatic transcription, chart recast or empirically validated rule promotion is claimed.
